summary: Outpost is an online game which enables children aged 7-12 years to run either a lunar  outpost. The players control all aspects of life support, energy supply, radiation shield, food and communication delay for a given mission. All resources compete against one another; hence, there is no room for any free choices. For instance, enhancing the shield before a solar storm means that the energy needed will be consumed by the greenhouse tonight. Solar storm events are derived from the NASA space weather data through DONKI, while the environment of each outpost is determined using NASA data for Moon missions. This solves the problem by turning mission requirements into a game format. It is important since it enables children to realize that survival in deep space involves intelligent decision-making and could motivate future scientists and engineers.
details:
What it does and how it works

The player gets to play in moon outpost for a number of mission days. Every day, the dashboard features the amount of oxygen, water, energy, food, radiation levels, and astronaut’s health. Different events like solar storm, dust storm or problems with equipment arise, and the player chooses how to allocate the available energy, resources, and astronaut time among the five systems. The outcome is calculated by the game simulator, and a debriefing screen explains the results based on scientific facts.

Benefits

• The way children learn about these kinds of limitations is from experience and not from studying about them in textbooks.

• No installation is needed since it functions on itch.io .

• Cards and easy-to-understand language make it appropriate for children aged 7 to 12 years old.

Intended impact

Our goal is for the child to complete the game and learn one truth about surviving in space: there will always be consequences to every decision, and engineers make the best trade-offs possible. We hope this encourages an interest in STEM and space exploration careers.

Tools and technologies

Use "Pygame and pygbag" Python for browser game; NASA DONKI (space weather) for any solar storm events; NASA OSDR for Astronaut’s health information; NASA Artemis missions for site information like days per year, temperature, light, and signal time; Ai agents; vs code

 

Creativity

In the game, you become the mission commander having to make real-life decisions every turn and not simply earning points. By making use of the real-life instances of solar storms, kids will be able to relive past space weather occurrences. The game will have the player make all decisions independently just like astronauts on Moon would do.

Factors our team considered

• Age appropriate: use of visuals, icons, and short descriptions.

• Scientific precision: actual NASA information rather than fabricated figures.

• Balance: No decision should always be the right one; therefore, all decisions have an actual trade-off.

• Accessibility: an online game which can run on any computer.

• Education beats Entertainment: each conclusion is based on a principle.
